Capture your screen, mark it up, record it. Everything runs on your own computer.

**New in this version:** live streaming gets a **live ink layer** (draw on the screen while you stream), **sound from one program** in a Studio scene, a **replay buffer** that saves the last 30 to 120 seconds with a hotkey, and **stream details** with warnings when the upload or the computer can't keep up; the editor can be used **fully from the keyboard** (F6 between parts, key tips with Alt on Windows); a new arrow or box **stays picked so you can adjust it**, shapes start where you press, and a **box highlighter** marks text; Windows follows the **system accent colour**; Linux dialogs belong to Snagster's window (inside it on Wayland), Screen captures on Wayland see **every screen**, and KDE Plasma shows Snagster's icon; macOS gets a **Settings toolbar**, capture keys that leave the Mac's own alone and **Quit & Reopen** after allowing Screen Recording; AI apps get clearer errors, a **free skill for coding agents** and one-click **MCP bundles**; and broken files no longer crash Snagster. The Mac app now needs macOS 12.3 or later. **New in 0.10.6:** on Linux with Wayland the desktop asks once to share the screen and remembers it (recording, streaming and screen captures no longer ask every time), hotkeys work through the desktop, Snagster follows the desktop's accent colour, and the Flatpak shows the screen in Studio; keyboard shortcuts now match the menus on every system (Ctrl+S saves, Ctrl+P prints), dialogs put their buttons in your system's order, screen readers can read the buttons, deleting from the Library moves to the Trash or Recycle Bin, Windows draws with Direct3D 12 (smoother on company laptops and in remote sessions), and AI apps can reach every option over MCP. **Fixed in 0.10.5 (Linux with Wayland, e.g. Ubuntu):** no more screenshot loop (Studio, recording and streaming use the desktop's screen sharing); a capture no longer seems frozen (the desktop's own screenshot tool picks the area); recording waits for screen sharing and its bar stays small. **New in 0.10.4:** a Flatpak download for Linux (`Snagster-linux-x86_64.flatpak`, the sandboxed Snagster for any distribution). **Fixed in 0.10.3:** Print Screen while Snagster is in the tray (the screen seemed frozen); updating when an older copy is still running ("Access is denied"); the Linux download now runs on Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13 and other current systems. **New in 0.10.2:** Linux works on Wayland desktops and inside a Flatpak (recording and live streaming use the desktop's own screen sharing, where you pick the screen); a Linux menu entry and store listing; `AI-DISCLOSURE.md` says which parts of Snagster are AI-generated. **New in 0.10.1:** Recent lists the pictures and videos you took before; capture a window from a list; one Snagster at a time; Settings and dialogs in their own centered windows; choose which graphics card encodes. **New in 0.10:** go live on several services at once (Twitch, YouTube and more) from one encode, up to 4K at 60 fps; Studio is the live workspace, with scene buttons and per-scene sound (up to 6 sources per scene) while you stream; choose the video encoder (or leave it on Automatic, which falls back by itself); NVIDIA graphics chips on Linux; the window never stops answering while it saves, exports or opens files; and `snagster --hw-report` to test graphics-chip encoding on your computer.

## Download

Pick your computer and click **Download**. Nothing to install.

| Your computer | Download | Then |
|---|---|---|
| 🪟 **Windows** 10 or 11 | **[⬇️ Download for Windows](https://github.com/SoloSaftis/Snagster/releases/download/__TAG__/Snagster-windows-x64-portable.zip)** | Open the downloaded folder and double-click **Snagster** |
| 🪟 **Windows**, Microsoft Store | **[Get it from the Microsoft Store](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9MVZGNTS547Z)** | Click **Get**; no security warning, and the Store keeps it up to date |
| 🍎 **Mac** with Apple chip (M1 or newer) | **[⬇️ Download for Mac](https://github.com/SoloSaftis/Snagster/releases/download/__TAG__/Snagster-macos-arm64.zip)** | Open the download and drag **Snagster** to Applications |
| 🐧 **Linux** | **[⬇️ Download for Linux](https://github.com/SoloSaftis/Snagster/releases/download/__TAG__/Snagster-linux-x86_64.AppImage)** | Right-click the file → Properties → allow running as a program, then double-click it |
| 🐧 **Linux, sandboxed** (Flatpak) | **[⬇️ Download the Flatpak](https://github.com/SoloSaftis/Snagster/releases/download/__TAG__/Snagster-linux-x86_64.flatpak)** | Run `flatpak install --user Snagster-linux-x86_64.flatpak`, then start Snagster from your apps menu |

## The first time you open it

The app is not signed yet, so your computer may warn you once:

- **Windows** says "Windows protected your PC": click **More info**, then **Run anyway** (the Microsoft Store edition doesn't ask).
- **Mac** says Apple "could not verify" Snagster: click **Done**, open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down and click **Open Anyway**. Then allow Snagster under **Screen Recording**.

## For AI apps

`Snagster-mcp-windows-x64.mcpb`, `Snagster-mcp-linux-x86_64.mcpb` and `Snagster-mcp-macos-arm64.mcpb` are MCP bundles (the Mac one for Apple silicon): AI apps that install bundles (such as Claude Desktop) add Snagster's tools in one step. `server.json` is the listing for the MCP Registry. With the normal download, Settings → AI apps shows the lines to copy instead.
